advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the added per-read signature-verify + compute_validity cost on default show/MCP/audit is acceptable, or cache/short-circuit when no plan-review attestation exists.
evidence: src/rebar/audit/read.py:73: verified = signing.verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review", repo_root=repo_root)
src/rebar/audit/read.py:80: result = attest.compute_validity(verified, ticket, "plan-review", repo_root=repo_root)
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:53: ticket["plan_review_health"] = plan_review_health(ticket)
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:189: out["plan_review_health"] = plan_review_health(state)
attest.compute_validity DEFAULT profile does dependency hashing (attest.py:645-660 `_hash_file(...)`) and material recompute (attest.py:673 `current_material_fingerprint`)
advisory.finding: Every detailed read path (default `rebar show`, MCP `show_ticket`, and `audit_trail`) now calls `plan_review_health`, which performs a full `signing.verify_signature` plus `compute_validity`; under the DEFAULT profile the latter re-hashes dependency files / HEAD and recomputes the material fingerprint. This adds non-trivial signature+IO work to hot read surfaces that previously did none of it.
scenarios: Listing/reading many tickets one-by-one via `rebar show <id> <id> ...`
MCP clients that call show_ticket frequently

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract the shared posture/no-related-material label derivation into one helper reused by CLI text, close-gate error, and (via context) the template.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py:211-228 posture + no-related-material block
src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:51-66 identical posture + no-related-material block
src/rebar/audit/templates/ticket.html:113-117 same logic in Jinja (`no_related_material`, `enforcement_disabled`)
advisory.finding: The posture (`enforced`/`enforcement disabled`/`advisory`) and `current (no related material)` derivation logic is duplicated verbatim in three places (CLI text renderer, close-gate error builder, and the Jinja template), so any future change to the presentation rules must be made in three synchronized locations.
scenarios: A later change to how disabled/advisory posture is labeled updates one site but not the others

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the plan_review_health import+assignment in reads_cli in the same best-effort try/except used for digest_freshness.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:179-186: `try: from rebar.llm.overlap import digest_sidecar ... except Exception: pass`
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:187-189: import + call sit after the except, ungated
comment at :177 `Lazy import + fail-safe so `rebar show` never breaks on it`
advisory.finding: In `reads_cli._cmd_show` the existing `digest_freshness` presentation call is wrapped in try/except so `show` never breaks, but the new `from rebar.audit.read import plan_review_health` import and call are placed OUTSIDE that guard. `plan_review_health` is internally fail-open, but the import statement is unguarded, unlike the sibling presentation-only enrichment right above it.
scenarios: Any import-time failure of rebar.audit.read (e.g. circular import during refactor) would break `rebar show` output where the neighboring enrichment is protected

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Format effective_execution_floor with the same %.2f precision in the close-gate error as in the CLI/web renderers.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:73-74: `detail += f"; floor={health['effective_execution_floor']}"`
src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py:237: `phase_line += f", floor={float(floor):.2f}"`
src/rebar/audit/templates/ticket.html:119: `floor: {{ "%.2f"|format(...) }}`
advisory.finding: The close-gate error detail formats the execution floor as a raw value (`floor={health['effective_execution_floor']}`) while the CLI text and web renderers format it as `%.2f`, producing inconsistent floor rendering across the three surfaces that the change explicitly intends to unify.
scenarios: A floor of 0.8 renders as `floor=0.8` in the close-gate message but `floor=0.80` in CLI/web

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that `compute_validity` health reports `advisory is True`, `enforcement_status == "disabled"`, `related_material_status == "pinned"` for the drift + enforcement-disabled case.
evidence: attest.py L563-567: `plan_health["advisory"] = bool(not enforced and plan_health["pin_status"] not in ("current", "current-no-relationships", "legacy-unpinned"))`
test_attestation_invalidation.py:255 `assert result["health"]["pin_status"] == "stale-pin-drift"` — this drift+disabled test asserts only pin_status

search of tests for `advisory` shows the only `health["advisory"]` assertion is `test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py:174 assert health["advisory"] is False` (the current-no-relationships case); NO test asserts `advisory is True`
advisory.finding: The advisory-drift behavior (the change's headline: enforcement-disabled drift becomes advisory, `plan_health['advisory']=True`) has no test assertion. The only test exercising the drift+enforcement-disabled path asserts solely `pin_status`, never `advisory`, `enforcement_status`, or `related_material_status`, so a regression on the new advisory flag would go undetected.
scenarios: A pinned prerequisite drifts while pin enforcement is disabled; operators expect the surface to read 'advisory; enforcement disabled'
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_attestation_invalidation.py::test_advisory_pin_health_preserves_existing_validity_keys, add: `assert result["health"]["advisory"] is True`, `assert result["health"]["enforcement_status"] == "disabled"`, `assert result["health"]["related_material_status"] == "pinned"`.
